# Pilot 3 failure tails

The four behavioral fixtures project T1's committed extraction at `96966f3ed8d4fbe06d9a3e8a6d7ca2e31633837d`. Their source entries identify the T1 fixture, pilot transcript, pilot usage file and frozen Eidos build by hash. Every retained response artifact was checked against the original SHA-256 blob, and each usage event was matched by sequence to the original transcript and by value to the exported usage file.

Each fixture preserves the final three turns' decision records, full response messages, per-request timestamps and associated usage events. Request prompts and earlier decisions are omitted. The three turns contain six runtime-origin deadline placeholders in each crash. N04-r2 also has one accepted decision immediately before the placeholders. The tests replay these messages with elapsed times, remaining times, request timeout and write margin scaled together. Read stubs return the original recorded read-receipt metadata. Historical effects stay offline.

When the corrected runtime admits a request that the historical runtime never sent, a clearly synthetic reply marks that divergence. The test preserves the observed refusal sequence so that the coordinator enters its one recovery. It supplies no historical recovery response, and the durable controller abstention preserves the failure and lock without asserting investigator completion or independent confirmation. The locked candidate used to exercise controller closure is synthetic.

The N02-r2 fixture preserves the terminal provider quota receipt from its verified transcript and usage files. The terminal request yielded no assistant reply. The coordinator test uses that receipt to reproduce the typed provider failure without external calls.

The separately identified N01-r2 Addendum 1 archive contains a completed arm-4 crash from an earlier attempt of the same block. Its source records the relative archive location, the block and arm attempt times, and the block record, run record, investigation, transcript and usage hashes. Its six replies and timing records come from the last three refused turns. Each response blob was verified by digest, and its transcript usage event was checked against the exported usage receipt and request IDs. Five historical decisions emitted deadline placeholders. The other decision proposed a wait directly, so it replays without a synthetic follow-up. The archived block remains excluded from pilot outcomes.

N03-r3, N04-r3, N01-r3 and N02-r2 record settled replacements under Addendum 7. Each run's last three refused turns contain six runtime-origin deadline placeholders. Each slot uses the SHA-verified historical response and matching usage receipt. A synthetic reply marks a newly admitted request that the historical runtime suppressed. The last N01-r3 slot leaves less than the durable-write reserve, so the corrected runtime reports deadline exhaustion without a follow-up, and the coordinator enters bounded finalization on that outcome. Earlier turns stay outside the replayed failure tail.

N02-r3 combines historical replies with a receipt-derived surrogate. Turn 9 slot 0 contains a model-authored wait and the following slots contain runtime deadline placeholders. Turn 9 slot 1 recorded two requests and a reasoning runaway at the output cap. The historical runtime counted the second request in usage and omitted the runaway reply from the serialized history. The fixture retains its receipt and the first reply and identifies the missing raw response by request ID. Two explicitly synthetic reasoning texts exercise the recorded runaway branch with the same finish reason, request ID and usage. The test checks identical billing, reads, follow-up admission and successor history, with both surrogate texts excluded from that history. The recorded decision elapsed time is a proxy for the missing provider timing. The coordinator continues the historical refusal sequence and enters bounded finalization. The other five slots replay all their historical replies. The original runaway text and exact request timing remain unavailable.
